summary: Emilio Teza (1831–1912) was an Italian scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Anton Boller. He served as a librarian at the Laurentian and Marciana libraries and held professorships at the universities of Bologna, Pisa, and Padua.

Emily T. Yeh (b. 1971) is a scholar of Tibetology who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. She joined the faculty at the University of Colorado around 2003.

Emma Georgina Rothschild (b. 1948) is an historian who studied at Somerville College, Oxford, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She held professorial appointments at the University of Cambridge (around 1991) and Harvard University (around 2008).

Emmanuel Levinas (1906–1995) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Strasbourg and under Martin Heidegger at Freiburg. He held posts at the universities of Poitiers (1961–1967), Paris (1973–1976), and Fribourg (1989–1991).

Emmie te Nijenhuis (b. 1931) is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, earning her PhD under Jan Gonda. She taught at Utrecht University and held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque (1937–2022) was a scholar of Indology and archaeology educated at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum and headed the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art.

Encho Tamura (1917–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Kyushu and Kyoto universities. He held academic posts at Kumamoto University, Kyushu University, and served as director of the Kyushu Historical Museum.

Endo Asai (1927–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served as a professor at Rissho University and as president of Minobusan University (1998–2001).
Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Mahidol University, supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.

Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He held posts as a professor at Otani University and as a lecturer at Kyoto University.

Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijō Tokiwa. He worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture and served as a professor at Otani University.

Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Francisco Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded Toyo University and served as a lecturer and manager there.

Ensho Kanakura (1896–1987) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University and Rissho University, and served as president of Miyagi University of Education.
Ensho Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University under doctoral supervisor Esho Mikogami and was attested as a visiting researcher there in 2007.

Enshu Kurumiya (b. 1942) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD under Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University.
Entai Tomomatsu (1895–1973) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Keio University and held a post at Taisho University.

Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a scholar of Tibetology and history who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London. He taught Tibetan language and literature at the University of Milan and held a post at the University of Bologna.
Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.

Eric Grinstead (1921–2008) was a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Victoria University of Wellington. He held posts at the British Library and the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies.
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Gary A. Tubb.
